in_sanskrit.name: बालकृष्ण
in_sanskrit.meaning: बाल (bāla) - child, कृष्ण (kṛṣṇa) - dark, black, and God Krishna
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Bāla (child) and Kṛṣṇa (dark, black, and God Krishna) make the name Balkrushna. Bāla refers to the child form of Lord Krishna, while Kṛṣṇa symbolizes the divine and powerful aspect of the deity.

historical_references.reference: Balkrishna was a prominent Maratha warrior and general during the reign of Chhatrapati Shahuji Maharaj (1707–1749). He was instrumental in the Battle of Pavan Khind and was awarded the title of 'Mastani Maharaj' for his bravery.

Balkrishna was also a significant leader in the Satara Kingdom during the late 18th century. He played a crucial role in the defense of the kingdom against the British East India Company and is remembered for his military strategies and leadership.
